new_statements.rule_in_words: Rengmitca is a lexical tone language (at least four tones: high level, checked high level, falling, checked falling) with extensive tone sandhi and sesquisyllabic (minor + major syllable) word shapes; the source makes no statement about word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone not verified for whole corpus; some grammatical markers left toneless; bare imperatives may shift stem tone. Nothing on stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements are transcription conventions for a text corpus in a morphosyntax paper, not a phonology section; the only dedicated description (Peterson 2013/2014, De Gruyter) could not be opened. Family-level surveys (Lotven 2023) characterise SC sesquisyllables as iambic weak-strong, but say nothing specific about Rengmitca.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the same variety: Rengmitca as spoken near Alikadam (Krangsi Para, Bandarban), fewer than 20 speakers shifting to Mru; no dialect differentiation reported. No ISO code; Glottolog reng1255.

sources.note: No statement on stress. Transcription note (fn.2, p.81) and fn.3 (p.82): Rengmitca has at least four lexical tones (high level, checked high level, falling, checked falling), extensive tone sandhi not yet understood, sesquisyllabic minor+major syllable structure; grammatical tone marginal (imperative tone shift).

sources.citation: Lotven, Samson. 2023. Tone in South Central Tibeto-Burman. Himalayan Linguistics 22(1): 36-66. doi:10.5070/H922153559
sources.note: Family-level survey; Rengmitca not discussed. General SC statement only: sesquisyllable = minor+major iambic (weak-strong) structure, minor syllables never word-final.
